student_materials.evaluations_note: This workbook contains 6 formal evidence tasks (E1–E6) plus a Final Mission. Each evidence is marked with a EVIDENCE flag. Your instructor will score these. All other activities are practice — they help you prepare.

student_materials.title: KWL Chart — The Diesel Workshop
student_materials.instructions: Fill in columns K and W today. You will complete column L in Session 8.

columns.heading: What I KNOW
columns.prompt: What do you already know about workshops and diesel engines? Write 3–5 ideas.

columns.heading: What I WANT to learn
columns.prompt: What do you want to learn in this guide? Write 3–5 questions.

student_materials.title: Gap Cards — Self-Rating Scale
student_materials.instructions: Rate yourself honestly from 1 (cannot do this yet) to 5 (can do this very well). Fill in the S1 column today. You will complete the S8 column in Session 8.
student_materials.scale: 1 = Not yet | 2 = A little | 3 = Sometimes | 4 = Usually | 5 = Yes, confidently

statements.statement: I can name 15 of the 20 key tools and areas of a diesel workshop in English.
I can classify types of maintenance (preventive, corrective, predictive) in English.
I can identify and report a safety hazard to my supervisor in English.
I can fill in a daily inspection checklist in English.
I can give basic instructions about PPE in English.
I can describe the current state of a service bay in English.
I can read a short article about workshop tools and understand the main ideas.
I can write a work order header with the correct fields in English.
I can use imperatives to give instructions (e.g., Check the floor jack.).
I can use 'There is / There are' to describe workshop conditions.
I can use prepositions of place (on, next to, near, under) correctly.
I can listen to a short dialogue and answer comprehension questions.
I can give a 60-second oral workshop readiness report in English.
I can request tools or help from a colleague in English.
I can confirm that I understood an instruction in English.
I can report the status of a bay to my supervisor in English.
I can pronounce 'fire extinguisher' and 'torque wrench' clearly.
I can pronounce 'preventive maintenance' and 'calibration' clearly.
I can complete a team workshop simulation using all 5 communication functions.
I can reflect on my English learning progress and identify areas to improve.

student_materials.title: What I Noticed Today
student_materials.prompt: Write 3–4 sentences about something you noticed or learned in today's session. You can write in English or Spanish.

student_materials.title: The Toolbelt 20 — Word Wall
student_materials.instructions: These are your 20 key words for the whole course. Study them. In the 'My Sentence' column, write your own sentence using each word.

student_materials.title: Cuestionario No 1 — Reading Comprehension
student_materials.instructions: Answer all 5 questions. Choose the correct option (a, b, or c) or write True / False. Work alone. No text during the quiz.

items.q: What does a torque wrench do?

options.b: It applies the correct force to a bolt

items.q: Why is the floor jack a safety tool?

options.c: Because it lifts the vehicle safely

items.q: Complete: 'The ratchet is fast in ___.'
What does calibration ensure?
True or False: 'A good technician never cleans the workbench.'

student_materials.title: Vocabulary Match — Column A / Column B
student_materials.instructions: Match each term in Column A with its correct definition in Column B. Write the letter on the line.

column_b.definition: A document describing a repair task
A tool that lifts the vehicle safely
Making sure a tool is accurate
A flat surface where you work
A list of items to verify
A fast tool for tight spaces

student_materials.title: Daily Inspection Checklist — Bay ___
student_materials.instructions: Complete all fields. Use Toolbelt vocabulary. Mark each item OK or Needs Attention. Write at least 2 observations.

student_materials.title: Work Order Header
student_materials.instructions: Complete all 6 fields in English. Use Toolbelt vocabulary.

student_materials.title: Lista de Verificación No 2 — Writing Self-Check
student_materials.instructions: Before you submit your Checklist and Work Order, check your own work. Mark YES or NO for each criterion.

criteria.criterion: My Daily Inspection Checklist has minimum 8 items verified.
Each item uses correct Toolbelt vocabulary.
I have written at least 2 observations in English.
The bay status is justified in English.
My Work Order has minimum 6 fields complete.
I used 'There is / There are' correctly in my observations.
I used imperatives correctly in required actions.
I used prepositions of place to locate tools.
The spelling of Toolbelt terms is correct.
My document is legible, organized, and complete.

student_materials.title: Stock Card A — Bay Status
student_materials.instructions: Choose your bay number and select the conditions. Use this card to prepare your Workshop Readiness Report.
fields: Tools on workbench: wrench / ratchet / socket / torque wrench
Floor jack: OK — no leaks / needs attention
Fire extinguisher: next to bay door / missing

student_materials.title: Stock Card B — Sentence Starters (Reference Card)
student_materials.instructions: Use these sentence starters to build your report. This card is pre-filled — it is a reference tool.
sentence_starters: Good morning. This is the Bay ___ Readiness Report.
There is a ___ on / under / next to ___.
The ___ is on / under / next to / near ___.
The floor is clean. / There is a spill near ___.
I check the ___. No leaks. The lift works.
Bay ___ is clean. Bay ___ is safe. Bay ___ is ready.

student_materials.title: Chunk Cards — Pronunciation Reference
student_materials.instructions: Practice saying each term using the chunks. Repeat each one 3 times.

cards.example: The fire extinguisher is next to the bay door.
Check the calibration of the torque wrench.
The torque wrench is on the workbench.
Check the floor jack. No leaks.

student_materials.title: Cuestionario No 3 — Listening Comprehension
student_materials.instructions: Listen to the Bay 2 Safety Briefing dialogue. Then answer these 5 questions. Work alone. No dialogue text allowed.

items.q: What does Carlos ask Valentina to put on first?
Where is the oil spill?
Where should the fire extinguisher always be?
How does Carlos say to check the floor jack?

options.a: Look for spills and clean it
options.b: Look for leaks and test the lift

items.q: What does Valentina say at the end?

student_materials.title: My Workshop Readiness Report — Preparation Outline
student_materials.instructions: Use Stock Card A and Stock Card B to build YOUR report. Write bullet points — not a full script. Practice speaking from these notes.

student_materials.instructions: Study these 5 communication functions. You will use all of them in the simulation.

functions.name: Describing Conditions

functions.name: Reporting to Supervisor
examples: There is a problem with the floor jack.

functions.name: Confirming Understanding
examples: Got it. I'll do it now.

student_materials.title: Cuestionario Consolidado No 6
student_materials.instructions: Answer all 25 questions. Choose the correct option (a, b, or c) unless the question says True or False. You have 90 minutes. No materials, no Word Wall, no Communication Card.

items.q: What is a 'workbench'?

options.b: A flat surface to work on

items.q: 'Hazard' means ___.
Which of these is PPE?
A 'work order' is ___.

options.a: an instruction to lift a vehicle
options.b: a document describing a repair task

items.q: 'Preventive maintenance' means ___.

student_materials.title: Final Mission Task Card — The Diesel Workshop Morning Briefing
student_materials.scenario: Monday, 7:00 AM. Bay assigned by instructor. The Workshop Training Coordinator arrives for the morning inspection. Your team of 3 delivers the complete Bay Readiness Briefing in English.
requirements: All 5 language functions visible — minimum instances per role as shown below
15 or more Toolbelt terms used across the team (each distinct term counts once)
Minimum 3 direct exchanges between team members (not 3 separate monologues)
There is/are + preposition in minimum 3 sentences
Minimum 2 imperatives from the Carlos role
Closing: 'Bay ___ is ready. Briefing complete.' or equivalent

responsibilities: Gives at least 2 instructions to the team (F1)
Confirms team readiness and closes the briefing
Describes bay conditions (F3 — There is/are + prepositions)
Requests tools or help from Santiago (F2)
roles_table.minimum_functions: F2 x1, F3 x2, F4 x1, F5 x1

responsibilities: Responds to tool/help requests from Valentina (F2 response)
roles_table.minimum_functions: F2 response x1, F3 x1, F5 x2

student_materials.instructions: Check the box when each evidence is complete and submitted.

student_materials.title: Appendix A — Toolbelt 20: Full Reference
student_materials.instructions: This is your complete vocabulary reference for the whole course. Study it. In the 'My Sentence' column, write your own sentence for each term.

functions.name: Giving Instructions / Dar instrucciones
functions.grammar: Imperative: base verb (no subject — 'you' is implied)
workshop_examples: Check the floor jack before lifting.
Clean the oil spill near the bay door.

functions.name: Requesting Tools / Help — Solicitar herramientas
key_phrases: Where is the ___? Can I use it?
workshop_examples: Can I have the torque wrench?
Where is the ratchet? Can I use it?

functions.name: Describing Conditions — Describir condiciones
functions.grammar: There is/are + noun + preposition of place
workshop_examples: There is a spill near Bay 1.
There are three tools on the workbench.
The floor jack is under the vehicle.

functions.name: Reporting to Supervisor — Reportar al supervisor
functions.grammar: Present Simple + There is/are — address supervisor by name
workshop_examples: There is a problem with the floor jack, Carlos.

functions.name: Confirming Understanding — Confirmar comprension
functions.grammar: Fixed expressions — vary them to sound natural
workshop_examples: Got it. I'll do it now.

student_materials.title: Appendix C — Your Evaluation at a Glance
student_materials.intro: This guide has 6 formal evidences plus a Final Mission. Here is what each one tests, when it happens, and how it is scored.

evidences.what: You read an article about diesel tools and answer 5 multiple-choice questions from memory.
evidences.conditions: No text during the quiz. 15 minutes.

evidences.what: You write a complete Daily Inspection Checklist (8+ items) and Work Order header (6 fields) for Bay 2.
evidences.conditions: Word Wall visible. 45 minutes. Individual work.

evidences.what: You listen to the Bay 2 Safety Briefing dialogue and answer 5 questions from memory.
evidences.conditions: No dialogue text. No Word Wall. 15 minutes.

evidences.what: You give a 60–90 second Workshop Readiness Report to the instructor (as supervisor) and answer 2 questions.
evidences.conditions: Word Wall visible. No notes in hand during performance.

evidences.what: Your team of 3 performs a 3–4 minute Workshop Opening Simulation using all 5 communication functions.
evidences.conditions: Word Wall visible. No notes during performance. Dual evaluation: instructor + peer.

evidences.what: 25 multiple-choice questions covering all 5 skills: Reading, Vocabulary, Grammar, Listening, Language Functions.
evidences.conditions: Closed materials. No Communication Card. No Word Wall. 90 minutes.

evidences.what: Your team delivers the complete Bay Readiness Briefing (3–4 minutes) with all 5 functions, 15+ Toolbelt terms, and team interaction.
evidences.conditions: Word Wall visible. No notes during performance. Instructor as Training Coordinator.
evidences.score: 5 points (6 criteria scored 1–5, holistic team score)
